newsitem.title: UK: BT unit to build Nigerian network.
newsitem.headline: BT unit to build Nigerian network.

text.p: A British Telecommunications (BT) subsidiary has won a contract to build and operate a high quality, reliable and low cost telephone network in Nigeria over the next five years, the company said on Thursday.
The BT Telconsult unit was awarded the contract for a one million fixed lines system by NITTI Company Ltd, which holds Nigeria's second national telecommunications operating licence.

"There is enormous unsatisified demand for telephone lines in Nigeria, " said Frank Day of BT Telconsult. "BT Telconsult and NITTI will be working together to provide customers with a significantly better quality of service," he added.
NITTI Company Ltd was set up in 1995 with the aim of becoming Nigeria's second national carrier. Its founders include key traditional leaders The Emir of Kano and The Ooni of Ife.

According to the country's National Communications Commission, there is a need for almost three million lines to meet both established and new demand in Nigeria -- which is the fourth largest oil producer in OPEC.
The country has only 0.2 lines per 100 people, even less than Ghana, which has 0.4, and Brazil, which has nine. The UK's "teledensity" is about 50 per 100 people.
BT, whose main planning team will arrive in Nigeria in late January, plans to install 150,000 lines during the first year.
